goal:
Lifty Life manages 22 homes in Harrison Hot Springs and 25 more in the surrounding region, and almost all of them are sold by someone else. In 2026, Airbnb produced 50 percent of Harrison revenue, VRBO 29 percent and Booking.com 9 percent. Direct bookings, through your website and Google Vacation Rentals, made up about 11 percent. At an average commission of around 15 percent, that mix sends roughly $100,000 a year to the platforms. You put the trade-off plainly: on a $1,000 booking, $150 goes to Airbnb, and a $50 cost to win that booking yourself would be a far better deal.

The goal you set for the Accelerator is to move Harrison direct bookings from about 11 percent toward 30 percent. That is the right destination, and on the coaching call you and Conner agreed it is a 2027 number rather than a 90-day one. Most of the direct bookings you get today are repeat guests who came back to save the service fees. Nothing currently gives a first-time guest a reason to choose Lifty Life over the same home on Airbnb, and most guests check out without knowing who Lifty Life is. The job of the next ninety days is to fix that: give booking direct a real set of benefits, put those benefits in front of every guest you are allowed to reach, and start buying the Harrison searches the big platforms ignore.

The plan does not ask you to build a members' portal. A "Lifty Life Member" for the next ninety days is simply someone on your email list who gets better terms when they book direct. A tag in your email platform and a custom field in Hostaway do the work a login system would do later. If the idea earns its keep, the portal becomes a sensible 2027 project with real member numbers behind it.

The order matters. Weeks 1 to 5 define the benefits and publish them on the website with a sign-up form, because every email and ad later in the plan points at that page. Weeks 3 to 11 build the follow-up that brings direct guests and members back for their next stay. Weeks 3 to 10 build an extended stays page and a small outbound list for the off-season, while the Agassiz pipeline work and insurance relocations are live demand. Google Ads tracking goes in during Week 2, and the campaigns switch on in Weeks 8 and 9, once there is a page worth sending people to and a way to count the bookings.

Stated honestly, the direct share will move slowly inside these ninety days. October to January is your quiet season in Harrison, and much of next summer gets booked in the spring. What the ninety days should produce is a member list that grows every week, the first next-year rebookings from guests who checked out this autumn, the first extended-stay bookings from outbound work, and a cost-per-booking figure from Google Ads you can compare against the $150 commission. Those are also the numbers that matter most for the part of the business you care about most. A property owner deciding between Lifty Life and another manager will be far more persuaded by "a growing share of our bookings come direct, and we fill your calendar in October" than by a lower fee.

weeks.title: Week 1: Decide the Benefits
actions: Write the member benefits list and settle the cancellation window and late checkout time
Adopt the "Lifty Life Member" name and draft the one-page guest services guide
Email the Airbnb and VRBO account managers with the plan and ask for written guidance, including on the existing Google review text
Reply to the most recent Google reviews, starting with the 4-star review about air conditioning
checklist: A written list of four or five member benefits exists, with specific terms
Questions are with both account managers in writing
The 4-star review and the ten most recent reviews have a personal response

weeks.title: Week 2: Hostaway and Tracking
actions: Create the "Lifty Life Member" custom field and the member automation in Hostaway
Add the GA4 Measurement ID to the Hostaway booking engine and configure both domains
Mark purchase as a key event and create the Hostaway custom definitions in GA4
Change the Google Business Profile primary category and fix the phone number mismatch
checklist: Guest services can see member status on every reservation
A test booking appears as a purchase in the GA4 Realtime report
The Google Business Profile category and phone number are correct

weeks.title: Week 3: Sign-Up Form and Baseline
actions: Write the Benefits page copy, including the comparison and FAQ
Build the member sign-up form with the CASL consent checkbox and connect it to the email platform
Set up the member, past direct guest, market and occasion tags
Export the baseline report and send it to Junction
Shortlist the homes that suit extended stays and confirm the Enbridge timing
checklist: Benefits page copy is complete and with whoever builds the page
A test sign-up arrives in the email platform tagged "member" with consent recorded
A dated baseline report exists and has been shared
An extended-stay shortlist of homes exists

weeks.title: Week 4: Benefits Page Goes Live
actions: Publish the Benefits page and add it to the main navigation and footer
Add the descriptor line and benefits strip to the homepage and update the meta title
Add the member message wherever the Hostaway booking engine allows custom content
Add the Occasion and Trip notes custom fields in Hostaway and brief guest services
Set the extended-stay minimum stay, payment terms and pricing rule
checklist: The Benefits page is live and reachable from every page of liftylife.ca
The homepage says "locally managed" above the fold
Guest services are recording occasions on new reservations
Extended-stay terms are written down

weeks.title: Week 5: Welcome Email and Pop-Up
actions: Build and test the first welcome email
Add the member sign-up prompt to liftylife.ca
Write the extended stays page copy and enquiry form
Ask owners of the shortlisted homes to confirm they will accept monthly guests
checklist: A new sign-up receives the welcome email within minutes
The sign-up prompt appears once per visitor and never on the booking engine
Extended stays page copy is written

weeks.title: Week 6: Extended Stays Page Live
actions: Build the Day 3, Day 7 and Day 14 welcome emails
Publish the extended stays page and redirect the older extended-stay pages to it
Set up the extended_stay_enquiry event and mark it as a key event
Set the Google Ads budget and write down the break-even cost per booking
checklist: All four welcome emails are live and send in order
The extended stays page is live with a working enquiry form
A test enquiry appears in GA4 as extended_stay_enquiry
The monthly ad budget and break-even figure are written down

weeks.title: Week 7: Post-Stay Thank-You and Outbound List
actions: Build the post-stay thank-you and Google review automation for direct and website channels only
Build the outbound list of 15 to 20 contacts and the one-page sales sheet
Create the Google Ads account in Expert Mode, link GA4 and import the three conversions
checklist: The thank-you email reaches a test direct reservation and no OTA reservation
An outbound list with named contacts exists, and the sales sheet is finished
Google Ads shows purchase, member_signup and extended_stay_enquiry as conversions

weeks.title: Week 8: Rebooking Email and Harrison Ads Launch
actions: Build the "Where to next?" rebooking automation
Send the first outbound emails with the sales sheet attached
Build and launch the Harrison accommodation campaign
Add the negative keyword list before the campaign spends
checklist: Direct guests receive the rebooking email three days after checkout
Every outbound contact has been emailed once
The Harrison campaign is live, with Display and search partners switched off

weeks.title: Week 9: Extended-Stay Ads and Annual Reminders
actions: Set up the ten-month anniversary and annual trip reminder in the email platform
Build and launch the extended-stay search campaign
Run the first weekly ads review and add negatives from the search terms report
checklist: Guests tagged with an occasion are scheduled for a reminder before next year's date
The extended-stay campaign is live and pointing at the extended stays page
The negative keyword list has grown from the search terms report

weeks.title: Week 10: Guest Guide and Follow-Ups
actions: Redesign the guest guide with the Lifty Life page and QR code, and place it in the ten busiest Harrison homes
Send the outbound follow-up emails
Run the weekly ads review
checklist: Ten Harrison homes have the new guest guide in place
Every outbound contact has had one follow-up, and outcomes are logged
The weekly ads figures are recorded in the sheet

weeks.title: Week 11: First Member Update
actions: Send the first monthly member update to the member and past direct guest tags only
Run the weekly ads review and pause keywords with 40 clicks and no conversion
Post a Google Business Profile update linking to the Benefits page
checklist: The member update has gone out, split by market where possible
No keyword has spent past 40 clicks without a conversion
The Google Business Profile shows a post from this month

weeks.title: Week 12: Review and Decide
actions: Compare every metric with the Week 3 baseline
Make the spring Google Ads budget decision and write down the numbers behind it
Count next-year rebookings, member sign-ups and extended-stay nights booked, and add them to the owner pitch
checklist: A 90-day report comparing every metric with the baseline exists
The spring ad budget decision is written down with the evidence behind it
Member count, rebookings and extended-stay nights are recorded for the 30-day and 60-day follow-up
